summary: The change does what the request asks. athena.toml sets [history] cutover_job to this job's id, and config.rs parses the field as optional. After `athena land --pr` writes the landing record, it calls a new cutover hook. The hook reads cutover_job from the athena.toml of the commit that just landed, takes C0 from that landing record, and appends one records commit: the import of records/ at C0 with import-manifest.json, plus legacy-exempt.json with 7 entries. The import then runs its self-check. The reconcile step that land and status run first repeats this as a catch-up, and it writes nothing on a second run. check_history switches to the new rules only when the records branch shows both the cutover landing and a manifest naming C0. Commits up to C0 are then judged by the old rules, using the legacy-exempt list, and later commits only by attribution. In every other case it runs exactly today's check, and when the landing exists but the import does not, it also prints a "pending" note. I ran the targeted tests myself in this snapshot and all passed: 8 cutover tests in athena-gate, 5 in athena-core, 1 in athena-data, and 3 catch-up tests. Athena's records show fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed. There are no blocker or major findings. The minor ones: three files outside the deliverables list were changed (reconcile.rs was planned); the CI change keeps the checkout token for every event; the records fetch is skipped on pull requests; and a successful cutover is reported in the land output's warnings list.
